t: Hormones are the universal villain — for both sexes
d: Cortisol, testosterone and peri-menopause do identical work across the set: they move the cause of a body the buyer dislikes from their behaviour to their biology. Happy Mammoth's 5 signs cortisol is controlling your body, Primal Queen's you're not broken … it's peri-menopause and Mars Men's no beer? no problem, cortisol's got your belly covered are one psychographic in three costumes: it isn't my fault, and the mechanism has a name.

t: GLP-1 is generating personas, not just demand
d: Four brands address four different people created by the same drug. Huel sells to the patient whose appetite vanished; Grüns to the one with constipation and sulfur burps; Primal Queen sells PQ7 as no injections, no jitters; Mars Men catches the man at before you start injections. Companion, side-effect fixer and refusenik are three separate buyers — treating GLP-1 as one audience leaves two of them unserved.

t: The heaviest spenders run the fewest ideas
d: RYZE keeps 80 distinct creatives alive that express only 3 concepts. Lineage runs 31 for 3. Flamingo runs 30 for 2. Volume advertisers vary the asset, never the argument — which is why their copy is useless for identifying a format and the composition has to be read instead. Watch the creatives→concepts column: a tight ratio marks a brand running a machine, not a test.

t: Medical-authority cosplay is the default proof device
d: Lab coats at Primal Queen and Resilia, Doctor Reacts at Ulike, from a real cancer researcher at Resilia, made by Yale-educated scientists at Thesis, and Primal Viking's my doctor told me something he'd never told a patient before. In none of these is the clinician the advertiser's own. The persona being served distrusts their actual doctor and trusts a credentialed dissenter.

We Made Too Much (Primal Viking), We really fcked up this time (Hismile), Apologies to last week's buyers (Mars Men), We're sorry — here's 55% off (Paleovalley). Framing the discount as a mistake or a logistics failure lets the price drop without conceding the product was ever worth less.

t: At the premium end, risk reversal replaced the discount
d: RŌZ's longest-running structure is a checkout screen reading Due Today $0.00 — only pay if your hair loves it. Norse Organics converts its returns policy into the efficacy claim: our return policy is simple. Acne will never return. Where price is the objection, the winning offer is don't pay yet, not pay less.
